elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: "Client may assign or transfer its rights under this Agreement without approval to an affiliate ..." — express no-approval affiliate right for Client (the prior "financially responsible" qualifier no longer conditions it).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "... without approval to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" — all three transaction types named, no approval required.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of Client"; the former mutual "financially responsible affiliate" no-approval exception is deleted, so no residual Vendor exception survives.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "... without the prior written approval of Client, which shall not be unreasonably withheld".

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "... and shall never assign to a competitor of Client" — unconditional bar, not subject to the consent standard.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "a change of control of Client shall give TrueLink no right to terminate this Agreement"; no other change-of-control or deemed-assignment language exists in the document to contradict it.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause gives the successor/M&A carve-out to Client only; TrueLink may assign only with Client's approval, so there is no Vendor successor right.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic appears in the rendered language; Client's successor assignment is simply "without approval" with no notice obligation.

The original mutual "Neither party shall assign ... without the prior written approval of the other party" was narrowed to TrueLink only, so Client's non-affiliate, non-successor assignments now require no consent at all.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Condition largely inapplicable: the only surviving consent requirement (on TrueLink assignments) is expressly qualified "which shall not be unreasonably withheld"; there is no other consent gate left to qualify.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: all six preferred elements are met in operative text (Client affiliate/successor carve-out without approval, Vendor assignment only with Client's approval not unreasonably withheld, absolute competitor bar, and express no Vendor termination right on Client change of control). Baseline was correctly assessed as a deviation — the original required TrueLink's approval for a Client merger or sale of substantially all assets, had an unqualified approval standard, and gave TrueLink the same no-approval affiliate exception.

Fallback level is incomplete (no Vendor successor right, no written-notice mechanic, no residual consent requirement on Client's other assignments), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met.

Minimality defect: converting "Neither party shall assign ... without the prior written approval of the other party" into a TrueLink-only prohibition deletes Client's own consent obligation for assignments outside the affiliate/successor carve-out. Nothing in the preferred checklist requires unrestricted Client assignment to any third party; the asymmetry needed is only the carve-out plus the Vendor-side consent standard and competitor bar. Repair by retaining a residual restriction on Client, e.g. add to the second sentence: "Client shall not otherwise assign or transfer its rights without TrueLink's prior written approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld."

Intent is preserved: no undefined terms, dangling cross-references, or contradictory retained sentences; the clause remains the sole assignment provision and no other commercial mechanic is disturbed.
Comment is accurate and matches the rendered text (no element merely promised in the margin).
